Carburetor icing can occur well above freezing temperatures when there is visible moisture or high humidity, because fuel vaporization and air expansion through the carburetor (Venturi effect) cause sudden cooling [20240614194471:factual][20190411X64435:factual][20230709192562:factual]. In several accidents, the weather conditions fell in the icing probability chart's regions of susceptibility, such as serious icing at glide power [20241026195377:factual][20190630X05538:factual] or serious icing at cruise power [20191204X11047:factual]. The bulletin advises pilots to check carburetor heat function before takeoff and to use carburetor heat on approach and descent at low power settings or when icing is probable [20190630X05538:factual][20240614194471:factual]. Warning signs are an rpm drop in fixed pitch propeller airplanes, a manifold pressure drop in constant speed propeller airplanes, and usually engine roughness [20240614194471:factual]."}
